summary: King County, WA pass lookout built 1934; airlifted in 1974 to Camp Waskowitz, where the tower is listed as standing; footings were seen at the pass site in 2014.

facts.status_note: Tower moved in 1974 to Camp Waskowitz near North Bend; Firelookout.org lists no tower at the original site

access.note: Drive-up site per WillhiteWeb; no gate or closure described, and no official access rule found. The road runs past a communication site, so confirm before visiting. Camp Waskowitz access not described.

visit.trail_note: Drive up, or hike the PCT from Stampede Pass (WillhiteWeb)

events.note: Built 1934 as a 40-foot timber L-4 tower; FFLOS and Firelookout.com give the same year, and WillhiteWeb agrees
Aircraft Warning Service used the site; a ground cabin was built; activated 14 Aug 1942, deactivated 15 Sep 1943
Airlifted by helicopter to Camp Waskowitz near North Bend. FFLOS and Firelookout.com say the tower moved; Forest Lookouts says only the cab did
A visitor reported at least two concrete footings still on the original site (a personal observation on a hobby site, not a survey)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and Firelookout.com say the whole tower was airlifted; Forest Lookouts says only the cab was airlifted and mounted on a new tower. The story reports both and does not pick one. Firelookout.org lists a standing tower at Camp Waskowitz either way.
FFLOS places the peak about 3/4 mile southeast of the pass; WillhiteWeb says a knoll south of the pass. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Brief record is largely right: relocated status, coordinates and elevation match Firelookout.com and Firelookout.org. Not verified in pages read: the FFLOS registration date (June 20, 2012) and the 'U.S. Forest Service' agency label; the agency fact here uses the national-forest name instead. Access is public only by inference from a hobby guide's drive-up directions and no closure; the road serves a communication site, so a reviewer may want to set this to permission. Today's condition of the Camp Waskowitz tower rests on the Firelookout.org index; no recent photo or camp access rule was read. Budget: 1 WebSearch and about 8 page reads, slightly over the per-tower limit because the 1974 move has conflicting sources.
